knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Without a confirmed limit from the material, the equipment rating or the authorised method, high pressure is not used. Cracked and loose areas are held and photographed. Option 0 and option 3 use pressure to beat a limit that is unknown, and option 2 still applies pressure to a roof with unassessed tiles.

Every hose, coupling and fitting must be rated at or above the equipment's maximum pressure and compatible with the set. Thread fit, price and appearance do not establish a rating, and a visual check once a year is not a pre-use check.

WorkSafe Victoria's alert says equipment and attachments must not be modified without written approval from the manufacturer or a competent person. Past use, telling the client afterwards, or a one-off trial do not replace that approval.

Water driven under laps is a sign of damage and a stop-work trigger. The worker stops, redirects the water away from the overlaps, and records the observation before any further work. Lowering the angle and continuing, raising the pressure, or ignoring it are unacceptable.

practicalCriteria: Using a paper job pack and photographs of a sample roof, the learner lists each roof material by plane, states the pressure or method limit source for each, and holds the pressure element where no limit is confirmed.

The learner completes an equipment pre-use check record for a sample set of hose, couplings, fittings and nozzle, states the rating of each part, and marks any unrated or faulty item as removed from use.
The learner records before-work photographs and a damage register for a sample roof, marking existing damage on laps, tiles and a rooflight before any water path is planned.
The learner states a stop-work decision for a sample roof that shows water being driven under laps and a cracked tile, and names the person to be informed and the next step.
passRule: Knowledge: all four checks correct. Practical: each of the four observable criteria met on the paper scenario, with zero critical safety failures, confirmed by an assessor. A pass on the paper exercise is not verified pressure-equipment competence and does not authorise operation.
evidenceRequired: Roof material register by plane, with the source of each method limit
Equipment pre-use check record with the rating of each part
Pre-work photograph set and damage register for the sample roof
Stop-work record naming the person informed and the next step
stopWorkCriteria: Authorises roof access, elevated work or climbing without competent approval
Ignores a fragile surface, skylight, electrical hazard or exposure to the public
Specifies unsanctioned chemical application, pressure settings or environmental discharge
Claims roof safety, compliance or specialist clearance without verified authority
Equipment is modified, or an unrated fitting is used, without written approval
A pressure setting is chosen without an authorised source or a confirmed material limit
Water is directed at laps, cracked tiles, sealant or a rooflight to test the result
